Market Notes

What we are seeing this quarter.

Short field reports from the agent collective. We file these from kitchens, gravel drives, and the occasional Amtrak station.

Inventory · Q2 Field Notes

Listings up north of Hudson, finally.

For two years, the corridor from Hudson up through Catskill and Athens behaved like a vault — almost nothing trading, prices held by sellers waiting for a number that never quite arrived. That changed in April. Six new listings on Warren and one of the better Athens river-block houses are now in play, and pricing has come down to within negotiating distance of last year's comps.

Eleanor Whitfield · 6 min read
Old Houses · Practice

Reading a slate roof from the driveway.

You can learn most of what you need to know about the state of an old roof before you ever climb on it. Look at where the slates are missing, look at where they have been replaced with the wrong color, look for the dark stain that means flashing has failed at a chimney. We walk through what to look for, and how to bring it up with a seller without scaring everyone off.

Owen Sato · 8 min read
Land · Hudson Valley

The case for the smaller working farm.

We have spent the last year showing more buyers a 6-to-12 acre property than any other category. People want enough land for a small orchard, a few animals, an honest vegetable garden — and they want it close enough to a village that bread is still a walk. The good news: this is more available, and more affordable, than the listings pages suggest.

Maya Bertrand-Cole · 5 min read
The Agent Collective

Six brokers. One brokerage. Every house treated like the only house.

We are a small bench by design. Every listing gets the attention of someone who has been doing this in the Hudson Valley for at least a decade — and every buyer gets a broker who actually picks up the phone.
